Title: GET /app/config works without a token and returns the default public settings
Preconditions: Fresh test database with all migrations applied and no rows in app_settings, so every setting is at its registry default. API started with APP_ENV=test.
Steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/app/config with no Authorization header and no X-App-* headers.
2. Send the same request again with the header Authorization: Bearer garbage.
3. Compare the body with the registry defaults in API_CONTRACT §6.
Expected result:
1. Both requests return 200 with a PublicAppConfig body and an X-Request-Id header. The bad token is ignored on this public route.
2. features: autoAssign false, transfers false, fuelRefills false, accessories false, support false, clientApp false, refills true, scanFlow false, confirmations false, dayEnd false, languageSwitch false.
3. minVersion is { driver: "0.0.0", distributor: "0.0.0" }; orders is { maxCylindersPerOrder: 30, deliveryStartedAt: "FIRST_LOAD_SCAN" }; refill.maxCylinders is 30; day is { timezone: "Asia/Karachi", cutoffLocalTime: "03:00" }.
4. Money is sent as digit strings: topup.minPaisa "50000", topup.maxPaisa "5000000", topup.quickAmountsPaisa ["200000", "500000", "1000000"], wallet.lowBalancePaisa "100000". wallet.capPaisa is null. topup.checkingHours is { from: "09:00", to: "21:00" }.
5. support is { phone: null, whatsApp: null, hours: "9am–9pm" }; environment is "test"; training is false; links.updateUrl is null.
6. The body holds no non-public setting: no lockedRoles, otpLogin, onAmountMismatch, maxPendingPerDistributor, secondApproval, refill deliveryCost or deliveryStrategy, and no company account title or IBAN.
Notes: The docs don't say a bad token on a public route is ignored; assumed, so a phone holding an old token can still read the update gate. topup.account is public only to distributors (served by GET /payments/topup-info, not here). Money fields in PublicAppConfig are assumed to follow §1.1 (digit strings).

Title: A settings change is audited and used by the very next request
Preconditions: Standard data. DA balance Rs 5,000. C1 "Sana" has a priced address in North. orders.maxCylindersPerOrder is at its default, 30.
Steps:
1. As SA1, GET /api/v1/settings and read the row for orders.maxCylindersPerOrder.
2. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/settings/orders.maxCylindersPerOrder with { value: 5, reason: "Rehearsal limit test" }. Note the X-Request-Id of the response.
3. Without a token, GET /api/v1/app/config.
4. As DA, POST /api/v1/orders with a new Idempotency-Key for C1 with one line of 6 × 11.8 kg (expectedReturnCount 6).
5. As DA, POST /api/v1/orders/quote for C1 with 5 × 11.8 kg.
6. As SA1, GET /api/v1/audit-logs?action=setting.update.
7. As SA1, PATCH the same key back to 30 with reason "Restore default after test".
Expected result:
1. Step 1: the row is { key: "orders.maxCylindersPerOrder", value: 30, default: 30, type: int, min: 1, max: 100, editable: true, public: true } with no updatedBy.
2. Step 2: 200 with the updated row: value 5, updatedBy SA1 ("Owner"), updatedAt set.
3. Step 3: orders.maxCylindersPerOrder is 5.
4. Step 4: 400 ORDER_TOO_MANY_CYLINDERS with message "Too many cylinders. An order can have at most 5." No order is created and DA's balance is still Rs 5,000 (GET /wallet balancePaisa "500000").
5. Step 5: 200 with quote.totalPaisa "45000" (Rs 250 + 5 × Rs 40 = Rs 450) and wallet.enough true.
6. Step 6: one setting.update row with actor { kind: USER, userId: SA1, name: "Owner" }, resourceType setting, reason "Rehearsal limit test", diff { key: "orders.maxCylindersPerOrder", from: 30, to: 5 } (resource_id is a UUID column, so the key is in the diff), and the requestId noted in step 2.
7. Step 7: the value is 30 again, and a second setting.update row records the change from 5 to 30.
Notes: SettingsService.set() clears the 30-second cache when it commits, and the pilot runs one API instance (ADR-23), so step 4 sees the new limit at once (API_CONTRACT §5.2). The details key behind {{max}} is max (§2.3).

Title: A refused settings change changes nothing and writes no audit row
Preconditions: All settings at their defaults, except topup.account, which the settings CLI set to the dummy company account (title "Smart Fleet (Pvt) Ltd", IBAN PK00TEST0000000000000000). Count the setting.update audit rows.
Steps:
1. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/settings/orders.maxCylindersPerOrder with value 0, then 101, then "abc", each with reason "Boundary test".
2. PATCH /api/v1/settings/orders.deliveryStartedAt with { value: "ON_DELIVERY", reason: "Bad value test" }.
3. PATCH /api/v1/settings/app.minVersion.distributor with { value: "1.0", reason: "Bad version test" }.
4. PATCH /api/v1/settings/orders.maxCylindersPerOrder with { value: 20 } and no reason; then with reason "abc" (3 characters).
5. PATCH /api/v1/settings/orders.notARealKey with { value: 1, reason: "Unknown key test" }.
6. PATCH /api/v1/settings/topup.account with another account ({ accountTitle: "Someone Else", bankName: "Other Bank", iban: "PK00OTHR0000000000000001", accountNumber: "1" }) and a reason. Then try pricing.deliveryStrategy, refill.deliveryCost, topup.secondApproval and auth.otpLogin.enabled { value: true } the same way.
7. As SA1, GET /api/v1/settings and GET /api/v1/audit-logs?action=setting.update. As DA, GET /api/v1/payments/topup-info.
Expected result:
1. Steps 1–3: 400 SETTING_INVALID_VALUE "This value isn't allowed here." for every request.
2. Step 4: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.fields naming reason, for both requests.
3. Step 5: 404 SETTING_UNKNOWN "Unknown setting."
4. Step 6: 403 SETTING_NOT_EDITABLE "This setting can't be changed here." for all five keys.
5. Step 7: every value is unchanged (maxCylindersPerOrder 30, deliveryStartedAt FIRST_LOAD_SCAN, app.minVersion.distributor "0.0.0", auth.otpLogin.enabled false). No new setting.update rows. DA still sees the account "Smart Fleet (Pvt) Ltd" with IBAN PK00TEST0000000000000000.
Notes: Each request carries one fault only, because the docs don't say which check wins when a body has both a bad value and a missing reason. The reason length 5–300 is from §7.13. The 1–100 range for maxCylindersPerOrder is taken as inclusive.

Title: The settings CLI sets the company account only with a reason, and logs it as System
Preconditions: Test server after the Inc 1 deploy. topup.account is not set. You can open a shell in the API container. DA is signed in on the shop app. SA1 is signed in on the website.
Steps:
1. On the phone, as DA, tap Add money.
2. In the API container, run the settings CLI (scripts/set-setting.ts) for topup.account with the value { accountTitle: "Smart Fleet (Pvt) Ltd", bankName: <test bank>, iban: "PK00TEST0000000000000000", accountNumber: <test number> }, without --reason.
3. Run the same command again, adding --reason "Owner's written request, dummy test account".
4. On the phone, go back and tap Add money again. Enter 5,000, tap Next and look at How to pay.
5. On the website, open Settings and find Company account. Then open the Activity log.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: the screen says "Top-ups aren't open yet. Call the office." and Next stays blocked.
2. Step 2: the CLI refuses with a one-line message that a reason is needed. Nothing is saved.
3. Step 3: the CLI says the setting was saved.
4. Step 4: the account card shows Account name "Smart Fleet (Pvt) Ltd" and the IBAN in groups of 4 ("PK00 TEST 0000 0000 0000 0000"), with "Copy IBAN" and "Copy amount".
5. Step 5: Company account is shown read-only, with no edit control. The Activity log has a row for the change with Who "System" and Why the reason from step 3.
6. In the database, that audit row has action setting.update, actor_kind SYSTEM, actor_user_id NULL and actor_label "cli:settings".
Spec ref: ADR-09; API_CONTRACT §2.3 (TOPUP_ACCOUNT_NOT_CONFIGURED), §5.2, §5.3, §6 (topup.account), §7.9, §8.5 (step 5); UX_MOBILE S3, S4; UX_ADMIN §2.8 (Company account), §2.9; Appendix B (setting.update)
Notes: The CLI's exact command line isn't documented; use the script's help text. The bank name and account number are dummy values (the standard data fixes only the title and IBAN). Grouping the IBAN by 4 is from UX_MOBILE S4.

Title: Errors use one envelope with a stable code, a plain message and the request id
Preconditions: Standard data. DA signed in.
Steps:
1. As DA, POST /api/v1/clients with { name: "", phone: "0300 7654321" } and an Idempotency-Key.
2. As DA, GET /api/v1/orders/<a random UUID that doesn't exist>.
3. As DA, GET /api/v1/no-such-route.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 400. The body has statusCode 400, code "VALIDATION_FAILED", error "VALIDATION_FAILED", message "Some details need fixing." (one string, not an array), details.fields with an entry { path: "name", code, message }, requestId equal to the X-Request-Id response header, path "/api/v1/clients" and an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp ending in Z.
2. Step 2: 404 with code NOT_FOUND and message "We couldn't find this. It may have been removed."
3. Step 3: 404 NOT_FOUND in the same envelope, not the framework's default body.
4. No body contains a stack trace, SQL, a file path or validator class names.
Notes: An unknown route answers 404 NOT_FOUND in the JSON envelope, like any unregistered path (API_CONTRACT §9.7). The format of details.fields[].path (dot-joined) isn't documented.

Title: The global error filter maps library and database errors to the documented codes
Preconditions: Unit test of the global exception filter and the central Prisma error filter, fed with fake errors. No database.
Steps:
1. Pass a ZodError for lines[0].fullCount and a class-validator error for name.
2. Pass a Prisma P2025 error.
3. Pass Prisma P2002 for each constraint in DATA_MODEL §7, and one for a constraint that isn't listed.
4. Pass Postgres CHECK violation 23514 on distributors_balance_chk, then on distributors_code_chk.
5. Pass P2002 on orders_distributor_id_client_request_id_key and on ledger_entries_idempotency_key_key.
6. Pass a plain Error, and AppError('PRICING_PRICE_NOT_SET', { zoneId, zoneName: 'East' }).
7. Pass Prisma P1001 and P2024, then P2034, then P2023.
Expected result:
1. Validation errors: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.fields [{ path, code, message }] for each field.
2. P2025: 404 NOT_FOUND.
3. P2002: payments_bank_reference_key_key → 409 TOPUP_BANK_REFERENCE_USED; distributors_home_store_id_key → 409 STORE_IN_USE; distributors_code_key → 409 DISTRIBUTOR_CODE_IN_USE; expense_types_name_key_key → 409 EXPENSE_TYPE_NAME_TAKEN; clients_distributor_id_phone_key → 409 CLIENT_PHONE_EXISTS; users_phone_key → 409 USER_PHONE_IN_USE; an unlisted constraint → 409 CONFLICT_DUPLICATE.
4. 23514: distributors_balance_chk → 409 WALLET_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE; distributors_code_chk → 400 DISTRIBUTOR_CODE_INVALID.
5. The client_request_id and ledger idempotency_key violations are not turned into HTTP errors: they reach the service as "already exists", so it can return the first record (200 with Idempotent-Replay) or the first result.
6. Plain Error → 500 INTERNAL_ERROR. The AppError → 422 with message "No delivery price is set for East yet. Ask the office to set it." and the same details.
7. Step 7: P1001 and P2024 → 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE; P2034 → 409 CONFLICT_STALE_STATE; P2023 → 404 NOT_FOUND. No body contains the raw error text.
Notes: distributor_zone_prices_distributor_id_zone_id_key needs "retry once, then 409 CONFLICT_STALE_STATE"; that retry lives in the pricing service and is tested there.

Title: The error catalogue is complete: a status, English text, documented parameters and an app key for every code
Preconditions: packages/shared-types/src/errors.ts exports ErrorCode, ERROR_HTTP and ERROR_MESSAGE_EN. The mobile errors resource and the admin-web errors namespace can be imported by the test.
Steps:
1. For every ErrorCode, read ERROR_HTTP and ERROR_MESSAGE_EN.
2. Compare the codes and statuses with a snapshot of the API_CONTRACT §2.3 tables.
3. Take every {{param}} from each English template and compare it with ERROR_DETAIL_KEYS in errors.ts and with the API_CONTRACT §2.3 details table (a key ending in Paisa maps to the name without the suffix).
4. Compare the mobile errors resource and the admin-web errors namespace with ERROR_MESSAGE_EN.
5. Search every AUTH_* message for the words "OTP" and "one-time code".
Expected result:
1. Every code has an HTTP status from 400 to 599 and a non-empty English message. Neither map has a missing or an extra key.
2. The statuses match §2.3, for example FEATURE_DISABLED 403, APP_UPDATE_REQUIRED 426, PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_DISABLED 410, FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED 415, FILE_TOO_LARGE 413, STORE_OUTSIDE_ZONES 422, TOPUP_ACCOUNT_NOT_CONFIGURED 503, RATE_LIMITED 429, CONFIRM_LINK_INACTIVE 410, DAY_SHEET_NOT_UPLOADED 409 ('Upload the filled sheet first.') and DAY_SHEET_OUTDATED 422.
3. Every {{param}} has a documented details key, for example WALLET_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE {{required}} and {{balance}} ↔ requiredPaisa and balancePaisa; AUTH_WRONG_APP {{app}} ↔ details.app; FILE_TOO_LARGE {{maxMb}} ↔ maxMb. ERROR_DETAIL_KEYS matches the §2.3 details table for every code.
4. The mobile resource and the admin-web errors namespace each equal ERROR_MESSAGE_EN plus the client codes NETWORK_OFFLINE, NETWORK_TIMEOUT and UNKNOWN (ClientErrorCode, §2.1) with the §2.3 client texts. The texts are imported, not copied.
5. No AUTH_* message contains "OTP" or "one-time code", in any letter case.
Spec ref: ADR-18; API_CONTRACT §2.1, §2.3, §8.6 (Shared rules), Appendix A; UX_MOBILE §3.2; UX_ADMIN §1.6, §1.7

Title: The app-version gate answers 426 below the minimum and compares versions as numbers
Preconditions: DA and DR1 signed in. app.minVersion.distributor and app.minVersion.driver at "0.0.0".
Steps:
1. As DA, GET /api/v1/distributor/home with X-App-Variant: distributor and X-App-Version: 0.1.0.
2. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/settings/app.minVersion.distributor to "0.2.0" with a reason.
3. Repeat step 1. Then repeat it with X-App-Version 0.2.0, and with 0.10.0.
4. Repeat step 1 with no X-App-Variant and no X-App-Version header, as the installed 0.1.0 app sends it.
5. As DR1, GET /api/v1/trips/mine with X-App-Variant: driver and X-App-Version: 0.1.0.
6. With no token and with X-App-Variant: distributor, X-App-Version: 0.1.0, GET /api/v1/app/config and GET /api/v1/health.
7. Set the minimum to "0.1.0" and repeat step 4. Then set "0.1.1" and repeat step 4.
8. Set the minimum back to "0.0.0" with a reason.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 200.
2. Step 3: 0.1.0 → 426 APP_UPDATE_REQUIRED "Please update the app to continue."; 0.2.0 → 200; 0.10.0 → 200 (compared as numbers, not as text).
3. Step 4: 426, because a missing version counts as 0.1.0.
4. Step 5: 200, because the driver minimum is still 0.0.0.
5. Step 6: 200 for both, so an old app can still read the gate and the support details.
6. Step 7: with minimum 0.1.0 → 200; with 0.1.1 → 426.
7. Step 8: all the calls above answer 200 again.
Notes: admin-web has no minimum key, so it is never gated.

Title: The shop app shows "Please update the app" when it is below the minimum version

Steps:
1. On the phone, open the menu, then Help. Write down the app version shown (for example 0.1.0).
2. On the website, open Settings > App versions. Set the shop app minimum one step above the phone's version (for example 0.1.1), with the reason "Update screen test".
3. On the phone, close the app fully and open it again.
4. Tap "Call the office".
5. On the website, set the shop app minimum back to 0.0.0 with a reason. Close the app and open it again.
Expected result:

Notes: Repeat the same check on the driver app with the driver minimum. The docs don't say what "Call the office" does when support.phone isn't set.

Title: An audit row is written in the same transaction as the change it records
Preconditions: DA balance Rs 5,000. The e2e app has a jest spy that makes AuditLogService.record throw for action wallet.correction.
Steps:
1. As SA1, POST /api/v1/admin/distributors/<DA>/wallet/corrections with Idempotency-Key K1 and { direction: "ADD", amountPaisa: 100000, reasonCode: "SYSTEM_ERROR", note: "Audit rollback test, please ignore" }.
2. As SA1, GET /api/v1/admin/distributors/<DA>/wallet and its statement.
3. Remove the spy. Send step 1 again with the same key K1.
4. Read the wallet, the statement and GET /api/v1/audit-logs?action=wallet.correction.
5. Clean up: TAKE Rs 1,000 with reason SYSTEM_ERROR and a note.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 500 INTERNAL_ERROR.
2. Step 2: balance still Rs 5,000 ("500000"); no ADJUSTMENT row; integrity ok.
3. Step 3: 201.
4. Step 4: balance Rs 6,000 ("600000"); exactly one ADJUSTMENT of +100000 with key adjust:K1; exactly one wallet.correction audit row, with actor SA1 and the reason code and note.
5. Step 5: balance Rs 5,000 again.
Spec ref: README rule 3; API_CONTRACT §3.1 (office overrides), §4, §5.1 (rules), §5.3, §5.4 (correct), §7.8 (corrections); DATA_MODEL §3.6 (Correction); Appendix B (wallet.correction)
Notes: Step 3 also proves that the failed first attempt didn't use up the key, because nothing was committed.

Preconditions: DA uploaded proof.jpg (fileId F1) as in FND-015.

2. Step 3: 404 FILE_NOT_FOUND "We couldn't find this file. Upload it again." for both (not 403), so the file's existence doesn't leak.

Title: Stored pictures are never public, and their links stop working after one hour

Title: A request that failed doesn't use up its Idempotency-Key (example X4)

Title: Two requests with the same key at the same moment make one order and one deduction
Preconditions: DA balance Rs 5,000. DA's prices are set in North.

Expected result:
1. In every run one response is 201 and the other is 200 with Idempotent-Replay: true, both with the same order id. Never a 500, and never two orders.

Title: A create answers 201 and its replay 200; every action sent as POST answers 200; no route answers 204
Preconditions: Standard test data. DA Rs 5,000 with a priced customer (Sana) and a top-up request P waiting. A small proof.jpg for the upload. Tokens for DA and SA1. A static scan of apps/api/src controllers is available to the test.
Steps:
1. As DA, POST /api/v1/orders (X1) with Idempotency-Key K1; send it again with K1. As DA, POST /api/v1/clients for a new customer with key K2; send it again with K2. 2. As DA, POST /api/v1/files/upload with proof.jpg; upload the same file again. 3. As SA1, POST /api/v1/admin/distributors//wallet/corrections (ADD Rs 100, reasonCode OTHER, a note) with key K3; send it again with K3. 4. POST /api/v1/auth/login as DA; POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with the refresh token. As DA, POST /api/v1/orders/quote for X1, then POST /api/v1/orders//cancel { reasonCode: "CUSTOMER_CANCELLED" }. 5. As SA1, POST /api/v1/payments/

/approve with a valid bank reference, amount and time. As DA, POST /api/v1/push-tokens { token: "ExponentPushToken[status-test]" }. 6. Scan the controllers for @HttpCode(204) and for handlers that answer 204.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: the first order and the first customer answer 201; each replay answers 200 with Idempotent-Replay: true and the same id.
2. Step 2: 201 both times; the second returns the existing fileId (same uploader, sha256 and purpose).
3. Step 3: 201, then 200 with Idempotent-Replay: true and the same entry id.
4. Step 4: sign-in, refresh, quote and cancel each answer 200, never 201.
5. Step 5: the approve answers 200 and the push-token register 200 { ok: true }.
6. Step 6: no route answers 204.
Notes: Nest answers 201 to every POST by default, so action routes need @HttpCode(200) (G15-03). Inc 2 and 3 action routes (stop and trip finish, case resolve, share, new link, day-end upload and submit) follow the same rule, and the public form POST /c/:token answers 303 (CNF-013).

Title: A list's cursor is refused by every other list and tab, and still pages its own list

2. Step 3: 200 with the other order and nextCursor null.
Notes: Regression case for review finding contract-compat-03 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV contract-compat-03 …". The cursor carries a tag of the list that made it: its path and its tab. A cursor issued before the tag existed gets this 400 once after the deploy. Unit tests: apps/api/test/unit/rev-cursor-lists.spec.ts.

Title: A deploy's shutdown lets a request in flight finish before the database closes
Preconditions: Standard test data. DA Rs 5,000. Another database session has locked DA's row, as a racing request would.
Steps:

2. Start the shutdown (app.close(), as a deploy's SIGTERM does), then release the lock 1.5 seconds later.
Expected result:

2. Step 2: the order answers 201 and is committed: one order, DA's balance Rs 4,520; the shutdown then completes.

Before the fix the order answered 503.

Title: A value Postgres can't store answers 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, never 500
Preconditions: Unit tests of the shared text and date schemas, the cursor decoder and the central error mapping.

2. Parse ISO instants in the year 0000 and with a six-digit year; decode cursors holding such dates.
3. Map data exceptions that still reach the database: P2010 with SQLSTATE 22021, 22P05, 22008, 22003 or 22001; P2000; P2033; "Could not convert argument value"; and 22P02.
Expected result:

2. Step 2: INVALID_DATETIME; each cursor gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on cursor.
3. Step 3: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.fields [], logged as a warning and not sent to Sentry; 22P02 stays 404 NOT_FOUND.
Notes: Regression case for review finding robustness-ops-06 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV robustness-ops-06 …". The routes are checked over HTTP by apps/api/test/review/robustness-ops/bad-input-500.e2e-spec.ts and fuzz-inc1.e2e-spec.ts: no 5xx anywhere.

Title: A body the parser refuses answers 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, logged at debug and never sent to Sentry

Notes: Regression case for review finding robustness-ops-07 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV robustness-ops-07 …". Title: While Redis is down, queue and worker errors are one warning a minute through the logger
Preconditions: The API booted as main.ts does, with REDIS_URL pointing at a port where nothing listens.

Preconditions: DA's user is ACTIVE and has a password. Use DA's sign-in number from the test data sheet.

2. Neither message contains "OTP" or "one-time code".

Spec ref: ADR-03; API_CONTRACT §2.1 (login wording), §2.3 (Auth and users), §7.1, Appendix A
Notes: +923009999999 is used only as a number that must not exist. Giving the same answer in both cases stops anyone finding out which numbers have accounts.

Title: Accounts that aren't active can't sign in

Title: Locked roles can't sign in, including the seeded branch admin

Title: Sign-in and token refresh are rate limited
Preconditions: Redis is up and the rate-limit keys are cleared. All requests come from one IP address.
Steps:
1. Send 5 sign-ins with DA's number and a wrong password within 10 minutes. Then send a 6th with the right password.
2. Move past the 10-minute window (advance the test clock, or clear the window key). Sign in with the right password.
3. From the same IP, send 30 sign-ins with 30 different unknown numbers within 10 minutes. Then sign in as DR1 with the right password.
4. Send 30 POST /api/v1/auth/refresh calls from one IP within a minute, then a 31st.
5. Stop Redis. Sign in as DA with the right password.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: attempts 1–5 get 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS. The 6th gets 429 RATE_LIMITED "Too many tries. Please wait {{minutes}} min and try again." with a number from 1 to 10 filled in, and no tokens even though the password is right.
2. Step 2: 200 with tokens.
3. Step 3: the 31st request gets 429 RATE_LIMITED.
4. Step 4: the 31st refresh gets 429 RATE_LIMITED.
5. Step 5: 200 with tokens: the guard lets requests through while Redis is down.
Notes: details.minutes is the whole minutes until the window resets, rounded up, at least 1 (API_CONTRACT §2.3). Every attempt counts, and a successful sign-in resets nothing (§3.6). With fixed windows the real wait can be shorter than 10 minutes.

Title: Code (OTP) sign-in is off, can't be switched on over the API, and never creates users

Title: Bad access tokens are refused, and reusing an old refresh token ends the session
Preconditions: DA can sign in. The test config gives one token a short access lifetime (for example 2 seconds).
Steps:
1. Call GET /api/v1/auth/me with: no token; "Bearer garbage"; a token signed with another secret; DA's token with the payload changed to role SUPER_ADMIN (old signature); an expired token.
2. Sign in as DA (refresh token R1). POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with R1 and note the new pair (A2, R2).
3. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh again with R1.
4. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with R2.
5. Sign in as DA again.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 401 AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID "Please sign in again." for every call. The edited token never reaches an office route.
2. Step 2: 200 with a new access token and a refresh token R2 that differs from R1.
3. Step 3: 401 AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID.
4. Step 4: 401 AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID, because the reuse revoked the whole chain.
5. Step 5: 200 with fresh tokens.
Spec ref: API_CONTRACT §2.3 (Auth and users), §3.3, §7.1 (POST /auth/refresh); UX_MOBILE §3.1 (single-flight refresh); UX_ADMIN §1.7
Notes: Reuse detection is today's behaviour (auth.service.ts:177-211), kept by §7.1. Because of it, both apps must refresh single-flight.

Title: The /drivers socket accepts only a valid driver or office session, and only the office hears locations
Preconditions: DR1 and DR2 ACTIVE and signed in; SA1 and DA signed in.
Steps:
1. Connect a socket.io client to the /drivers namespace with no auth.token; then with "garbage"; then with an expired token.
2. Connect with DA's access token.
3. Connect DR1, DR2 and SA1 with their own tokens.
4. DR1 emits location:update { lat: 31.5204, lng: 74.3587 }.
5. As SA1, suspend DR1 with a reason. Wait 60 seconds. DR1 reconnects with the old token.
Expected result:
1. Steps 1–2: the server emits error { code } and disconnects: no token, "garbage" and the expired token get { code: 'AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID' }; DA gets { code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED' }. No drivers:snapshot is sent.
2. Step 3: DR1 and DR2 stay connected (room driver:<id>). SA1 stays connected (room office) and receives drivers:snapshot.
3. Step 4: SA1 receives driver:location for DR1. DR2 receives nothing.
4. Step 5: the reconnect gets error { code: 'AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED' } and a disconnect.
Spec ref: API_CONTRACT §3.3, §7.14, §8.6 (Access: a socket without a token is disconnected), Appendix A
Notes: The event name driver:location is today's (drivers.gateway.ts:51). An open socket whose session ends is dropped with error { code } (API_CONTRACT §7.14): a driver's socket on its next message; the office's socket at once for a change made through the API, within 60 seconds for a change made elsewhere, and when its access token expires. Tests: apps/api/test/security/rev-live-sessions.e2e-spec.ts and apps/api/test/review/security/office-socket-and-tracking.e2e-spec.ts.

Title: A driver's location is taken only from that driver's own session
Preconditions: DR1 and DR2 online on the socket. DR2's last location is a known point L2 in Lahore.
Steps:
1. DR1's socket emits location:update { driverId: <DR2>, lat: 31.5204, lng: 74.3587 }.
2. DR1's socket emits online:set { driverId: <DR2>, isOnline: false }.
3. DR1 emits three location updates within 5 seconds.
4. As DR1, PATCH /api/v1/drivers/<DR2>/location with { lat: 31.5, lng: 74.3 }, and PATCH /api/v1/drivers/<DR2>/online.
5. As SA1, GET /api/v1/drivers/<DR2> and /drivers/<DR1>.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: DR1's location becomes 31.5204, 74.3587. DR2 stays at L2. The office broadcast names DR1.
2. Step 2: DR1 goes offline; DR2 stays online.
3. Step 3: only one update in those 5 seconds is stored and broadcast.
4. Step 4: 404 NOT_FOUND for both. DR2's location and online state don't change.
5. Step 5: DR2 is at L2 and online.
Spec ref: API_CONTRACT §7.2 (PATCH /drivers/:id/location, /online: DRIVER exact, own id), §7.14, §8.6 (Access: a driver can't move another driver's location)
Notes: An ownership miss answers 404 NOT_FOUND (API_CONTRACT §3.2). What happens to extra updates within 5 seconds (dropped quietly or refused) isn't documented.

Title: No response anywhere contains a password hash, a CNIC or a token hash
Preconditions: Seed with CNICs and passwords on DA, DB, DR1 and DR2. X1 assigned to DR1, so the order has a driver.
Steps:
1. Crawl every GET route in the Nest router as SA1, DA, DB and DR1, filling path ids from the seed.
2. Also capture the bodies of POST /auth/login, POST /auth/refresh, PATCH /users/me, POST /drivers and POST /distributors, and the drivers:snapshot socket event.
3. As DA, GET /api/v1/orders/<X1>.
Expected result:
1. Steps 1–2: no key named passwordHash, cnic, cnicEncrypted, cnicIndex, codeHash or tokenHash at any depth, and no value that looks like a CNIC (13 digits, or 5-7-1 digits with dashes).
2. Step 3: trip.driver is exactly { id, name, phone }.
Notes: The value check catches a CNIC that slips out under another key name. Office views may carry cnicMasked (for example '*****-****567-1'), which passes the value check: it is neither 13 digits nor 5-7-1 digits (API_CONTRACT §3.5).

Title: CORS answers only our own website's origin
Preconditions: API started with CORS_ORIGINS set to the test website's origin only (for example https://office.test.smartfleet.example).
Steps:

Expected result:

Title: The API refuses to start in production or staging with default secrets or test switches
Preconditions: Unit test of the boot-guard function that main.ts calls before NestFactory.create. process.exit and the logger are mocked. Each variant starts from a fully valid production env.
Steps:

With NODE_ENV=production, change one value at a time: JWT_ACCESS_SECRET = "change_me_access_secret_but_long_enough"; JWT_ACCESS_SECRET 31 characters long; JWT_ACCESS_SECRET equal to JWT_REFRESH_SECRET; DATABASE_URL missing; REDIS_URL and REDIS_HOST both missing; BULLMQ_PREFIX "smartfleet"; the S3 keys set to the minio defaults; CORS_ORIGINS "*"; ENCRYPTION_KEY missing; ENCRYPTION_KEY of 63 hex characters; BLIND_INDEX_KEY missing.
2. With NODE_ENV=production, add one at a time: AUTH_EXPOSE_OTP=true, TEST_PHONES=…, ALLOW_DEMO_SEED=true, SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD=…, PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_ENABLED=true.

5. Step 5: 403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE "This account isn't active. Call the office."
6. Step 6: both get 403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE, as on live. (On the test server these two may be reactivated afterwards as test logins.)
7. Step 7: a user.create_office row for Owner and one for Ops, and the three changes of step 3 with their reasons.
Notes: Don't copy the default passwords into the test sheet; read them from the seed file. The actor of user.create_office (SYSTEM with a cli label) isn't documented.

Title: Only the super admin changes a role, with a reason and an audit row, and unsafe changes are refused
Preconditions: The seeded "LPG Branch Admin" (ADMIN, no driver or shop profile). DR2 has a driver profile. SA1 and DA are signed in.
Steps:
1. As DA, PATCH /api/v1/users/<Branch Admin>/role with { value: "DISPATCHER", reason: "Role change test" }.
2. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/<SA1>/role with { value: "DISPATCHER", reason: "Self change test" }, and PATCH /api/v1/users/<SA1>/status with { value: "SUSPENDED", reason: "Self suspend test" }.
3. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/<Branch Admin>/role with { value: "SUPER_ADMIN", reason: "Promote test" }.
4. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/<DR2>/role with { value: "DISTRIBUTOR", reason: "Profile mismatch test" }.
5. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/<Branch Admin>/role with { value: "DISPATCHER" } and no reason.
6. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/<Branch Admin>/role with { value: "DISPATCHER", reason: "Role change test for audit" }. Read the audit log and the user's token_version. Then change the role back to ADMIN with a reason.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.
2. Step 2: 403 USER_SELF_CHANGE_NOT_ALLOWED "You can't change your own account this way." for both requests.
3. Steps 3–4: 403 USER_ROLE_CHANGE_NOT_ALLOWED "This role change isn't allowed."
4. Step 5: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, naming reason.
5. Steps 1–5 change nothing and write no user.role_change or user.status_change row.
6. Step 6: 200. The role is DISPATCHER, token_version goes up by 1, and one user.role_change row holds actor SA1, the reason, and before ADMIN / after DISPATCHER.
Spec ref: ADR-02; API_CONTRACT §2.3 (Auth and users), §3.1, §3.3, §7.2 (PATCH /users/:id/status, /role); Appendix B (user.role_change, user.status_change)
Notes: Every pilot user has a profile that fixes its role, so a valid change is rare in the pilot; this case uses the seeded ADMIN user, which has no profile. Moving between two locked roles keeps that account unable to sign in.

Title: Two super admins suspending each other at the same time can't lock the office out
Preconditions: SA1 and SA2 are the only ACTIVE super admins, and both are signed in.
Steps:
1. At the same moment (Promise.all), SA1 sends PATCH /api/v1/users/<SA2>/status { value: "SUSPENDED", reason: "Race test A" } and SA2 sends PATCH /api/v1/users/<SA1>/status { value: "SUSPENDED", reason: "Race test B" }.
2. Count the ACTIVE SUPER_ADMIN users and the user.status_change audit rows.
3. Reactivate the suspended one (through the database or the CLI) and repeat 20 times.
Expected result:
1. In every run exactly one request succeeds (200) and the other gets 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED: both lock the active super-admin rows and re-read the caller, so the second sees that its sender was just suspended.
2. After every run at least one super admin is ACTIVE, and that run wrote exactly one user.status_change row.
Notes: USER_LAST_SUPER_ADMIN stays as the safety net; with the lock it can't happen in this race (API_CONTRACT §7.2).

Title: A user can change only their own name and email; phone, CNIC and business name are office-only
Preconditions: Standard test data. DA and DR1 signed in. Note DA's users row (name, email, phone, CNIC, business name) and token_version.
Steps:

2. As DA, PATCH /api/v1/users/me { phone: "0321 7654321" }; then { cnic: "35202-1234567-1" }; then { businessName: "Ahmed Gas & Sons" }.
3. As DA, PATCH /api/v1/users/me { name: "Ahmed", phone: "0321 7654321" } (one allowed and one office-only field together).
4. As DR1, PATCH /api/v1/users/me { phone: "0333 1112222" }.
5. As DA, GET /api/v1/users/me. Read DA's users row again.

Spec ref: ADR-02; API_CONTRACT §2.3 (USER_FIELD_OFFICE_ONLY), §3.5, §7.2 (PATCH /users/me), Appendix A (GET/PATCH /users/me: phone edit refused); UX_MOBILE S12 (read-only Profile)

Title: The office resets an app password: old sessions end, it is audited, and unsafe targets are refused
Preconditions: Standard test data. DA signed in on a phone (tokens A1 and R1). A CLIENT test user exists. SA1 and SA2 signed in. Note DA's token_version.
Steps:
1. As SA1, POST /api/v1/users/<DA user id>/password with the new password "NewShop#2026".
2. As DA, call GET /api/v1/wallet with A1 every 10 seconds for 70 seconds. Then POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with R1.
3. Sign in as DA with the old password, then with "NewShop#2026".
4. As SA1, POST /api/v1/users/<SA2 user id>/password with "Office#2026x". Then POST /api/v1/users/<CLIENT user id>/password with "Client#2026x".
5. As DA, POST /api/v1/users/<DR1 user id>/password with "Driver#2026x".
6. As SA1, POST /api/v1/users/<SA1 user id>/password with "Owner#2026x".
7. As SA1, GET /api/v1/audit-logs?action=user.password_reset.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 200 { ok: true }, and DA's token_version goes up by 1.
2. Step 2: A1 is refused with 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED within 60 seconds, and the refresh is refused with 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED.
3. Step 3: the old password gives 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS; the new one gives 200 with tokens.
4. Step 4: both 403 PERMISSION_DENIED (the office sets app passwords for distributors and drivers only). SA2's and the client's passwords are unchanged.
5. Step 5: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.
6. Step 6: 403 USER_SELF_CHANGE_NOT_ALLOWED (an office user changes their own password with POST /auth/change-password).
7. Step 7: exactly one user.password_reset row, for DA, with actor SA1. No password or hash appears in the row or in any response.
Spec ref: ADR-02; API_CONTRACT §3.3, §3.5, §7.2 (POST /users/:id/password: office; not a CLIENT; another super admin's password only by themselves; bumps tv; audited), Appendix B (user.password_reset); UX_ADMIN §2.4 (Set app password)

Title: Driver profiles: the office sees and edits them; a driver sees only their own and changes only name and photo
Preconditions: Standard test data. DR1, DR2, SA1 and DA signed in. Note DR1's phone.
Steps:
1. As DR1, GET /api/v1/drivers/<DR1 id>; then GET /api/v1/drivers/<DR2 id>.
2. As DA, GET /api/v1/drivers and GET /api/v1/drivers/<DR1 id>.
3. As DR1, PATCH /api/v1/drivers/<DR1 id>/profile { name: "Kashif Ali" }; then { phone: "0300 5556667" }; then PATCH /api/v1/drivers/<DR2 id>/profile { name: "X" }.
4. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/drivers/<DR1 id>/profile { name: "Kashif" }.
5. As DR1, PATCH /api/v1/drivers/<DR1 id>/vehicle and PATCH /api/v1/drivers/<DR1 id>/availability with valid bodies.
Expected result:

2. Step 2: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED for both.
3. Step 3: the name change is 200. The phone change gives 403 USER_FIELD_OFFICE_ONLY "Ask the office to change this." and the phone is unchanged. DR2's profile gives 404 NOT_FOUND and is unchanged.
4. Step 4: 200, with a driver.update audit row holding the before and after names.

Spec ref: ADR-02; API_CONTRACT §3.5, §7.2 (GET /drivers, GET /drivers/:id: office or the driver reading themselves; PATCH /drivers/:id/profile: a driver on themselves, name and photo only; /vehicle, /availability: office), Appendix B (driver.update)

Title: A user can remove only their own push token
Preconditions: DR1 and DR2 signed in. DR2 has registered the push token "ExponentPushToken[dr2-test]" with POST /api/v1/push-tokens.
Steps:
1. As DR1, POST /api/v1/push-tokens { token: "ExponentPushToken[dr1-test]" }.

3. As DR1, DELETE /api/v1/push-tokens { token: "ExponentPushToken[dr1-test]" }.
4. Read the push token rows.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 200 { ok: true }, and one row exists for DR1's user.
2. Step 2: 200 { removed: 0 }; DR2's token is not removed.
3. Step 3: 200 { removed: 1 }; DR1's token is removed.
4. Step 4: DR2's token row is still there and still belongs to DR2's user.
Spec ref: API_CONTRACT §7.2 (POST /push-tokens: signed in, own; DELETE /push-tokens: deletes only the caller's own token)
Notes: Today the route deletes anyone's token.

Title: Alert rules are office only, and a 'credit over' rule can't be created
Preconditions: Inc 1 build after inc1a. Fixture: one DISTRIBUTOR_CREDIT_OVER alert rule from before the switch-over.

Title: The website signs the office out after 30 minutes without activity, with a warning at 28
Preconditions: Signed in to the office website as Owner on a laptop. A watch or the laptop clock to time the steps.
Steps:
1. Open Top-up requests and leave the laptop untouched for 28 minutes.
2. Move the mouse, then leave the laptop untouched again for 30 minutes.
3. Read the page you land on.
4. Sign in again.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: at 28 minutes a toast says "You'll be signed out in 2 minutes. Keep working to stay signed in."
2. Step 2: moving the mouse restarts the timer; after 30 more idle minutes the website signs you out.
3. Step 3: the sign-in page says "You were signed out after 30 minutes without activity." It never says "10 minutes".
4. Step 4: sign-in works.

Title: Tracking shows the shop its driver's position only while its order is on the way
Preconditions: Standard test data with cylinders. DR1 and DR2 report positions (PATCH /drivers/:id/location).
Steps:

4. Place three more orders: one cancelled before loading, one failed after leaving the store, one reassigned from DR1 to DR2 before loading. As DA, GET each tracking; then DR2 departs the store stop and DA reads the reassigned one again.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: DA gets the same keys as before (orderId, status, destination, driver, driverLocation, tripId, paymentStatus, deliveryFeePaisa), with driverLocation null while ASSIGNED; SA1 gets the position.
2. Step 2: stage ON_THE_WAY with TRACK offered, and DA gets DR1's position.

4. Step 4: the cancelled and the failed order give driverLocation null; the reassigned one names DR2 with driverLocation null until DR2 departs the store, then DR2's position, never DR1's.
Notes: Regression case for review finding security-01 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV security-01 …". Accepted for the pilot (API_CONTRACT §7.6): while its order is on the way, the shop also sees the driver when he serves another distributor's trip at the same time. Confirming test: apps/api/test/review/security/office-socket-and-tracking.e2e-spec.ts.

Title: An open office socket on /drivers ends with its session or its token, and a driver's socket is re-checked on every message
Preconditions: Standard test data. SA1 and SA2 connected to the /drivers socket and received drivers:snapshot.
Steps:
1. As SA1, change SA2's role (PATCH /users/<SA2>/role { value: "ADMIN", reason }).
2. SA1 changes its own password (POST /auth/change-password) and opens a socket with the new access token; then its sockets are re-checked.
3. Suspend SA2 outside this API (a database change the session cache isn't told of). Run the office re-check at once, then again 61 seconds later.
4. DR1 connects with a token that expires in 2 seconds; 2.5 seconds later it sends location:update.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: SA2's socket gets error { code: 'AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED' } and is disconnected at once.
2. Step 2: the socket of the old token is dropped with AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED; the one opened with the new token stays connected through the re-check.
3. Step 3: the first re-check keeps SA2's socket (the session row is cached for up to 60 seconds, API_CONTRACT §3.3); the one 61 seconds later drops it with AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED. SA1's socket stays.
4. Step 4: DR1 gets error { code: 'AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID' } and a disconnect, and his position isn't stored.
Notes: Regression case for review finding security-02 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV security-02 …". An office socket also gets an expiry timer when it connects: apps/api/test/review/security/office-socket-and-tracking.e2e-spec.ts checks that a suspended office user and an expired office token stop hearing driver positions. The website half (refresh and reconnect) has its own case in the OFF area.

Title: A DISTRIBUTOR or DRIVER caller without its profile id is refused at every scoped route, before any read
Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA without its distributorId), DRIVER (DR1 without its driverId)
Preconditions: Standard test data with X1 assigned to DR1. Callers carry DA's and DR1's user ids and roles but no profile id, as a legacy user with no distributors or drivers row would.
Steps:

Expected result:

2. Step 2: all three are refused with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.
3. Step 3: DR1's own trip only.
Notes: Regression case for review finding security-03 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV security-03 …". Such a user also gets no tokens: sign-in 403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE, and refresh and every request with an old token 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED; the office can't give it a password or make it ACTIVE (apps/api/test/review/security/profileless-role-token.e2e-spec.ts). A unit test scans every route and service for an unchecked cast of the caller's id (apps/api/test/orders/review-fixes.spec.ts).

Title: A driver whose user isn't ACTIVE can't go online, and nothing changes

Title: While a module is off, a GET of one record answers 403 FEATURE_DISABLED, lists keep [], and next suggestions leave out transfers

Title: CORS_ORIGINS must be real website origins: the templates' placeholder is refused, and the Caddyfile serves the hosts the apps call

Title: Low-balance flag follows wallet.lowBalancePaisa and is true only below it
Role: Developer (API test) as SA1, DA and DB
Preconditions: Standard test data. DA Rs 5,000, DB Rs 0. wallet.lowBalancePaisa at its default 100000 (Rs 1,000).
Steps:
1. As DB, GET /wallet.
2. As SA1, record a correction on DA: TAKE 400000, reasonCode OTHER, note 'test setup low balance' (DA now Rs 1,000). As DA, GET /wallet.
3. As SA1, TAKE 100 more (DA now Rs 999). As DA, GET /wallet.
4. As SA1, PATCH /settings/wallet.lowBalancePaisa {value: 50000, reason: 'test lower warning'}. Right after it, as DA GET /wallet.
5. GET /app/config without signing in. Then set the setting back to 100000 with a reason.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: DB lowBalance true (Rs 0 is below Rs 1,000).
2. Step 2: DA at exactly Rs 1,000: lowBalance false.
3. Step 3: DA at Rs 999: lowBalance true.
4. Step 4: with the threshold at Rs 500, DA at Rs 999: lowBalance false. An audit row setting.update records {key: 'wallet.lowBalancePaisa', from: 100000, to: 50000} with the reason and actor SA1.

The shop app shows the card 'Your balance is low. New orders need enough money for the delivery cost.' with 'Add money' whenever lowBalance is true (UX_MOBILE S2).

Title: orders.deliveryStartedAt = DRIVER_ASSIGNED or LEFT_STORE moves the refund cut-off
Role: SA1, distributor DA and driver DR1 (API)
Preconditions: Standard test data. DA has enough balance. Each scenario uses a fresh X1.
Steps:
1. As SA1, PATCH /settings/orders.deliveryStartedAt {value: 'ON_DELIVERY', reason: 'bad value test'}.
2. Set DRIVER_ASSIGNED (with a reason). A: cancel an unassigned X1. B: cancel an X1 right after assigning DR1.
3. Set LEFT_STORE. C: assign, load-scan, then cancel. D: assign, load-scan, DR1 fails it (CUSTOMER_REFUSED). E: assign, load-scan, depart the store stop, then cancel.
4. Set FIRST_LOAD_SCAN. Assign a fresh X1 to DR1. Switch to DRIVER_ASSIGNED, then cancel it. Restore FIRST_LOAD_SCAN.
5. GET /app/config after each change.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 400 SETTING_INVALID_VALUE; the setting is unchanged.
2. A: refund Rs 480. B: refund Rs 0 with noRefundReason 'DELIVERY_STARTED'.
3. C: refund Rs 480 (loading alone doesn't count under LEFT_STORE). D: 409 ORDER_NOT_STARTED_USE_CANCEL. E: refund Rs 0.
4. Step 4: refund Rs 0; the audit row shows startedRule 'DRIVER_ASSIGNED' (the rule is read when cancelling).
5. Each change writes setting.update {key, from, to} with the reason; /app/config orders.deliveryStartedAt shows the current value.
Spec ref: ADR-07; API_CONTRACT §5.2, §5.5, §6, §7.6, §7.13, Appendix B; UX_ADMIN §2.8; UX_MOBILE S9 (refund sentence)
Notes: The shop app's refund sentence must follow the value: orders.new.refundRule.DRIVER_ASSIGNED ('…If you cancel before a driver is assigned, you get it back…') and LEFT_STORE ('…If you cancel before the van leaves your store…'); 'Check and place' reads the app config fresh (FEE-007). The rule isn't stored on the order (DECISIONS ADR-07), so E4 is the documented behaviour.

Title: OrdersFeePolicy: delivery-started and cancel-terms rules
Preconditions: OrdersFeePolicy with OrderForPolicy fixtures; WalletService mocked.
Steps:
1. Run isDeliveryStarted for each rule (FIRST_LOAD_SCAN, DRIVER_ASSIGNED, LEFT_STORE) against: nothing set; assignedAt; IN_TRANSIT with onTheWayAt only; loadStartedAt; store stop departedAt; delivery stop arrivedAt; status DELIVERED; status FAILED.
2. Run cancelTerms for: DEDUCTED and not started; DEDUCTED and started; DEDUCTED with fee_strategy LEGACY_ZONE_PAIR (charged by the old code) and not started; fee status NONE (an order from before the switch-over, or a zero cost) not started; a terminal status; handoverStarted true.
3. Call cancel for a NONE order and for the legacy DEDUCTED order, and check WalletService.reverse.
Expected result:
1. FIRST_LOAD_SCAN is started by loadStartedAt, departedAt, arrivedAt, DELIVERED or FAILED, never by onTheWayAt alone; DRIVER_ASSIGNED adds assignedAt; LEFT_STORE ignores loadStartedAt.
2. cancelTerms: refundPaisa = the fee only for DEDUCTED and not started; 0 with noRefundReason 'DELIVERY_STARTED' once started; 0 for NONE; 0 with noRefundReason null for the legacy DEDUCTED order; allowed false for a terminal status or a started hand-over.
3. For the NONE order and the legacy DEDUCTED order no reversal is written: reverse is never called for the legacy order, and it returns null when there is no ledger row keyed order:<id>:debit.
Spec ref: ADR-07; API_CONTRACT §5.4 (reverse), §5.5, §8.1 (orders before the switch-over); DATA_MODEL §3.4 (backfill 3)

2. As DA, GET /pricing/quote for a vertex of North that touches no other zone.
3. As DA, GET /pricing/quote five times for a vertex shared by North and South.
4. As DA, GET /pricing/quote for the Outside point.
5. As SA1, GET /zones/locate for the same five points.
Expected result:
1. Every call in steps 1-4 returns 200 (the quote never errors for coverage).
2. Inside North: zone North and blockCode null. Inside South: zone South and blockCode null.
3. North's outer vertex: zone North (border points count as inside).
4. Shared vertex: the same single zone all five times, namely the one with the smaller area (if the areas are equal, the one created first, then the lower id).
5. Outside: serviceable false, zone null, price null, blockCode "PRICING_ZONE_NOT_COVERED".
6. GET /zones/locate gives the same zone for each point, and no zone for Outside.
Notes: Use exact polygon vertices: points in the middle of an edge suffer floating-point error. The response shape of GET /zones/locate isn't in the docs; compare the zone id only.

Title: A pin in an archived zone counts as outside, and quotes re-check the zone instead of trusting the saved one
Preconditions: Isolated fixture. Sana's (C1) address was saved with zone North. No open order exists for Sana. DA and SA1 tokens.
Steps:
1. As SA1, archive zone North (DELETE /zones/{northId}).
2. As DA, GET /pricing/quote at Sana's pin.
3. As DA, POST /orders/quote { clientId: Sana, addressId: Sana's North address, deliveryLabel: "House 14, Street 5", lines: 2 × 11.8 kg (take back 2), 1 × 45.4 kg (take back 1) }.
4. As DA, GET /clients.
5. As SA1, PATCH /zones/{northId}/reactivate. Then repeat step 3.
Expected result:
1. Step 2 returns 200 with zone null and blockCode "PRICING_ZONE_NOT_COVERED".
2. Step 3 returns 422 PRICING_ZONE_NOT_COVERED with the message "This location is outside our delivery area." Nothing is written (it's a quote).
3. Step 4 shows Sana's address with zone null and priceStatus "OUTSIDE".
4. After reactivating, the quote returns 200 with quote.zone.name "North" and quote.totalPaisa "48000" (Rs 250 + 2 × Rs 40 + Rs 150 = Rs 480).
Spec ref: ADR-08; API_CONTRACT §5.6, §7.4 (priceStatus), §7.5 (orders/quote), §7.2 (zones archive and reactivate); DATA_MODEL §3.2 (ClientAddress.zoneId: the order re-checks), §6 (6)
Notes: While North is archived every North order is blocked, so run this in its own fixture. Archiving North doesn't move Ahmed Gas Store: a store's zone is recomputed only when the store is edited. DA's North price row is kept and applies again after the reactivation (API_CONTRACT §7.2, §7.4).

Title: Ahmed Gas can never see or use Bilal Gas's customers; the office only reads customers, by distributorId

Title: Only the office adds, archives and reactivates zones, and a broken shape is refused
Preconditions: Standard test data. Prepared GeoJSON: a MultiPolygon "West Test" that overlaps no zone, a self-crossing (bow-tie) shape, and an empty MultiPolygon.
Steps:
1. As DA, POST /api/v1/zones with West Test.
2. As SA1, POST /api/v1/zones with the bow-tie shape; then with the empty MultiPolygon.
3. As SA1, POST /api/v1/zones with West Test.
4. As SA1, DELETE /api/v1/zones/<West Test id>, then send the same DELETE again. As DA, GET /api/v1/zones/locate for a point inside West Test. As SA1, GET /api/v1/zones/city/<Lahore id>?includeArchived=true.
5. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/zones/<West Test id>/reactivate. As DA, repeat the locate.
6. As SA1, POST /api/v1/zones with West Test's shape, the name 'Nowhere Test' and a random cityId.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.
2. Step 2: 400 ZONE_INVALID_SHAPE "This zone shape isn't valid." for both; no zone row and no audit row are written.
3. Step 3: 201 { id }; the zone is active, and one zone.create audit row by SA1.
4. Step 4: the first DELETE gives 200 { ok: true } and one zone.archive audit row; the second gives 200 with X-Already-Applied: true and no second row. The locate finds no zone for the point (archived zones are left out), and the office list with includeArchived shows West Test as archived.
5. Step 5: one zone.reactivate audit row; the locate finds West Test again.
6. Step 6: 404 NOT_FOUND with details.field 'cityId'; no zone row is written.
Spec ref: API_CONTRACT §2.3 (ZONE_INVALID_SHAPE), §7.2 (POST/PATCH/DELETE /zones, PATCH /zones/:id/reactivate: office; valid non-empty MultiPolygon; GET /zones/locate; includeArchived); DATA_MODEL §6 (6: active zones only)
Notes: The setup CLI's shape checks are SET-004.

Title: Order lines need at least one full cylinder, one line per size, and at most orders.maxCylindersPerOrder cylinders (default 30)

7. As SA1, PATCH /settings/orders.maxCylindersPerOrder { value: 40, reason: "Test bigger orders" }. Then repeat step 5, and quote one line of 31 × 15 kg.

9. As DA, quote one line of 11.8 kg with fullCount 101.
Expected result:
1. Steps 1-3: 400 ORDER_LINES_INVALID with the message "Add at least one full cylinder, one line per size."
2. Step 4: 200 with quote.totalPaisa "40000" (South is flat).

Spec ref: API_CONTRACT §7.6 (body, rule 3), §7.5 (quote uses the create validation), §6 (orders.maxCylindersPerOrder), §5.2 (30 s cache), §2.3; DECISIONS defaults table
Notes: The body schema runs first: no lines, a fullCount below 1 or a repeated size is ORDER_LINES_INVALID (API_CONTRACT §7.6, §2.2). A single line may carry up to the setting (the body allows 1-100 per line).

Title: Placing an order creates exactly one order, even after a double tap or a lost signal
Preconditions: Shop app signed in as Ahmed Gas. Usman (South, Rs 400 flat) exists. Note how many orders My orders → Active shows. Note the balance on Home. A developer is on hand for step 6.
Steps:
1. Tap New order → Usman → 3 × 15 kg → Next → Check and place. Tap "Place order · pay Rs 400" twice, quickly.
2. Read the screen that opens. Then open My orders.
3. Start another order for Usman with 1 × 15 kg and go to Check and place. Switch on airplane mode. Tap "Place order · pay Rs 400".
4. Read the screen. Switch airplane mode off. Tap "Try again".
5. Open My orders → Active.
6. With a developer's help, start one more order for Usman (1 × 15 kg), cut the network right after tapping "Place order · pay Rs 400" (the server gets the order but the phone gets no reply), then reconnect and tap the button again.
7. Open Wallet history and count the new "Delivery cost" rows.
8. Clean up: open each of the three new orders and cancel it (reason Other, note "Test order").
Expected result:
1. Step 1: the button shows a spinner and ignores the second tap. The order screen opens with the title "Order AG-…" and the message "Order placed · Rs 400 paid". It says "The office will assign a driver." and never "A driver will be assigned shortly".

5. Step 5: exactly one new 1 × 15 kg order for Usman (not two), whether or not the first attempt reached the server.
6. Step 6: the second tap shows the same order with "Order placed · Rs 400 paid" once; My orders has one order from that attempt, not two.
7. Step 7: exactly three new "Delivery cost" rows of −Rs 400, one per order placed in this case.
Spec ref: API_CONTRACT §4 (2), §1.2; UX_MOBILE S9 (submit, success), §2.2 (Button double-tap guard, ErrorBanner, OfflineBanner), §3.1 (one key per intent), §3.5, §6 (a retry never creates a second order)

Title: Delivered guard: only the trip's driver can mark an order delivered, and only once, even with a double tap or two taps at once

3. Step 3: T1 isn't an active trip for DR1; GET /orders/{X1} gives 404 NOT_FOUND; the PATCH gives 404 NOT_FOUND (the same as his GET); the scan gives 409 SCAN_TRIP_CLOSED and AG-C0001 stays in Ahmed Gas Store.

Spec ref: ADR-12; API_CONTRACT §7.6 (assign-driver rules 4-5, PATCH status), §8.1, §8.3, §3.2 (canSeeOrder); UX_ADMIN §2.9 (order.reassign sentence)
Notes: Whether /trips/mine still lists aborted trips (marked aborted) isn't specified; assert only that T1 isn't active.

Title: Changing the driver is refused once a cylinder is loaded, and the office can't abort that trip
Preconditions: X1 is assigned to DR1 on trip T1. AG-C0001 (11.8 kg, full) is at Ahmed Gas Store. Tokens for SA1 and DR1.
Steps:
1. As DR1, POST /custody/scan { qrCode: "AG-C0001", eventType: "SCAN_OUT", tripId: T1 }.
2. As SA1, GET /orders/{X1}.
3. As SA1, POST /orders/{X1}/assign-driver { driverId: DR2, reason: "Test" }.
4. As SA1, PATCH /trips/{T1}/status { status: "ABORTED", reason: "Test abort" }.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: AG-C0001 moves to van LEA-101, and X1 gets loadStartedAt with stage LOADING.
2. Step 2: allowedActions doesn't include REASSIGN.
3. Step 3: 409 ASSIGN_ORDER_LOADED with details.plateNo "LEA-101" and the message "Cylinders are already loaded on LEA-101, so this order can't change driver." T1 and its stops are unchanged and no new trip exists.
4. Step 4: 409 TRIP_INVALID_TRANSITION.

Title: A driver change racing the first load scan: either the change wins or the load wins, never both
Preconditions: X1 is assigned to DR1 on trip T1; nothing is loaded. AG-C0002 is full at Ahmed Gas Store. Tokens for SA1 and DR1.
Steps:
1. At the same moment: SA1 POST /orders/{X1}/assign-driver { driverId: DR2, reason: "Race test" } and DR1 POST /custody/scan { qrCode: "AG-C0002", eventType: "SCAN_OUT", tripId: T1 }.
2. Read X1, T1, any new trip, and where AG-C0002 is.
3. Reset the fixture and repeat 20 times.
Expected result:
1. Either the change wins: the reassign returns 200, T1 is ABORTED with its stop CANCELLED, the scan is refused with 409 SCAN_TRIP_CLOSED, AG-C0002 stays in Ahmed Gas Store and X1 has no loadStartedAt.
2. Or the load wins: the scan succeeds (AG-C0002 on LEA-101, X1 has loadStartedAt), the reassign returns 409 ASSIGN_ORDER_LOADED, and T1 stays open.
3. Never both: a 200 reassign together with AG-C0002 loaded on LEA-101 for an aborted trip.
Spec ref: ADR-12, ADR-13; API_CONTRACT §4 (1: lock rows first), §7.6 (assign-driver rule 4), §7.7 (custody/scan common checks); DATA_MODEL §3.6 (the first load scan locks the trip's orders)
Notes: Both the reassign and the load lock X1's order row first (API_CONTRACT §7.6 assign-driver rule 1, §9.2 step 3; DATA_MODEL §3.6), so these are the only two outcomes.

Title: Two office users assigning the same order at once, or one user submitting twice, leave exactly one live trip

3. SA1 sends the same assign of O2 to DR1 twice in a row.
4. As DR1 and as DR2, GET /trips/mine.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: both calls may return 200 (one as an assign, the other as a reassign), or one may fail. In every case O1 ends with exactly one trip that isn't ABORTED and exactly one DELIVERY stop that isn't CANCELLED.
2. The audit log has one order.assign row and at most one order.reassign row for O1, matching the final driver.
3. Step 3: the first call returns 200 (order.assign); the second returns 200 with X-Already-Applied: true and the same tripId. O2 has exactly one live trip, with DR1, one order.assign row and no order.reassign row.
4. Step 4: each driver sees only live trips; nobody sees an aborted trip for O1 or O2 as active.

Title: A driver sees and acts on only their own trips and orders
Preconditions: X1 is assigned to DR1 on trip T1. DR2 has no trips. AG-C0003 is full at Ahmed Gas Store. Tokens for DR1 and DR2.
Steps:

3. With no token: GET /trips/{T1}.
Expected result:

2. DR1: /trips/mine lists T1; GET /trips/{T1} returns 200 with stops[].status and allowedActions.
3. No token: 401.
Spec ref: ADR-02; API_CONTRACT §3.2 (canActOnTrip, canSeeOrder), §7.7 (trips, custody/scan: the trip is the caller's), §8.6; Appendix A
Notes: Every ownership miss answers 404 (API_CONTRACT §3.2), so another driver's arrive gives 404 too.

Title: Trip and stop steps in Inc 1: start, arrive, depart, finish and office abort
Preconditions: O1 and O2 (DA) are each assigned to DR1, on trips T1 and T2, both PLANNED. Tokens for DR1 and SA1.
Steps:
1. As DR1, PATCH /trips/{T1}/status { status: "IN_PROGRESS" }.
2. As DR1, PATCH /trips/stops/{T1's store stop}/arrive twice, then /depart twice.
3. As DR1, PATCH /trips/{T1}/status { status: "COMPLETED" } while O1 isn't delivered.
4. As DR1, mark O1 delivered, then PATCH /trips/{T1}/status { status: "COMPLETED" }. Send the COMPLETED again.
5. As SA1, PATCH /trips/{T2}/status { status: "ABORTED" } with no reason; then with reason "Van broke down".
6. As DR1, PATCH /trips/{T1}/status { status: "PLANNED" }.
7. As SA1, send the abort of T2 again, with the same reason.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: T1 is IN_PROGRESS with startedAt set; O1 stays ASSIGNED (stage DRIVER_ASSIGNED, onTheWayAt null): starting a trip never moves its orders.
2. Step 2: arrive sets the stop ARRIVED, and the second arrive returns 200 with X-Already-Applied: true and keeps the same timestamp; depart sets it DONE with completedAt, and the second depart returns 200 with X-Already-Applied: true and changes nothing. After the first depart of the store stop, O1 is IN_TRANSIT with onTheWayAt set (stage ON_THE_WAY).
3. Step 3: 409 TRIP_ORDERS_OPEN ("Finish or close every order on this trip first.").
4. Step 4: 200 and T1 is COMPLETED; the second PATCH COMPLETED returns 200 with X-Already-Applied: true.
5. Step 5: without a reason, 400 VALIDATION_FAILED; with the reason, 200 and T2 is ABORTED (nothing had happened on it). O2 is PENDING with trip null, assignedAt null and stage NEEDS_DRIVER; both stops of T2 are CANCELLED; one trip.abort audit row by SA1 with the reason and orderIds [O2]; no ledger row.
6. Step 6: 409 TRIP_INVALID_TRANSITION.
7. Step 7: 200 with X-Already-Applied: true; no second trip.abort row.

Title: Cancelling an order cancels its stop; the trip is aborted only if nothing was loaded
Preconditions: O1 is assigned to DR1 on trip T1, nothing loaded. O2 is assigned to DR1 on trip T2, and AG-C0004 has been load-scanned on T2. DA and SA1 tokens.

2. T1 is ABORTED and O1's DELIVERY stop is CANCELLED.
3. T2 is not aborted (it has a load scan); O2's DELIVERY stop is CANCELLED; AG-C0004 is still on van LEA-101.
Spec ref: API_CONTRACT §7.6 (cancel step 6), §8.3; DATA_MODEL §3.6 (Cancel step 5); API_CONTRACT §9.8 (a cylinder loaded for a cancelled order stays on the van)
Notes: Whether the cost comes back (X3) is asserted in the money cases.

Title: Assign and change driver on the website: no store picker, no automatic option, and the trip starts at the shop's store

Title: A hand-back of an earlier run's empties doesn't block a driver change or keep an idle trip open; a cylinder handed to the customer does
Preconditions: Standard test data with cylinders. DR1's and DR2's vans each still carry a cylinder left from an earlier run.
Steps:
1. As DA, place X1; as SA1, assign DR1 (trip T). As DR1, POST /custody/scan { eventType: "SCAN_IN", tripId: T } for the leftover empty. As SA1, GET /orders/<X1> and GET /trips/<T>.

4. Place a third order and assign DR1; DR1 scans the full cylinder left on his van to the customer (DELIVERED, no load on this trip). As SA1, GET the order, then try assign-driver to DR2.
5. Place a fourth order and assign DR1; before loading anything, DR1 takes back a cylinder Sana kept from an earlier delivery (PICKED_UP_EMPTY). As SA1, GET the order, then try assign-driver to DR2.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: X1 stays ASSIGNED with loadStartedAt null and a Rs 480 refund on offer, and allowedActions includes REASSIGN; the trip's own allowedActions are [] (the office abort still needs a trip with no event at all).
2. Step 2: 200 with reassignedFromTripId T; T is ABORTED and X1 is on DR2's trip.

5. Step 5: loadStartedAt is still null, REASSIGN is not offered, and assign-driver gives 409 ASSIGN_ORDER_LOADED: REASSIGN is offered exactly when rule 4 accepts the change.
Spec ref: ADR-12; API_CONTRACT §1.6 (REASSIGN), §7.6 (assign-driver rule 4, cancel step 6), §7.7 (PATCH /trips/:id/status ABORTED); DATA_MODEL §3.6
Notes: Regression case for review finding contract-compat-02 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV contract-compat-02 …". Before the fix any cylinder event blocked a driver change, and the 409 said cylinders were loaded when none were.

Title: Expense field rules: amount, date (judged in Asia/Karachi), note, and a van and driver that exist

Steps:

5. POST /expenses with a random vehicleId; then with a random driverId.

Expected result:

Spec ref: ADR-14, ADR-21; API_CONTRACT §7.12 (POST /expenses rules), §1.1 (whole rupees, plain YYYY-MM-DD dates), §2.2, §2.3
Notes: Step 3 is after the 03:00 business-day cut-off and step 6 before it, where the calendar date and the business date differ. Expense dates are plain Asia/Karachi calendar dates (API_CONTRACT §1.1, §7.12).

Expected result:

Title: After creation: the code can change only before the first order, the store can't be removed, and activate and suspend are audited
Preconditions: City Gas (CG) from OFF-004, with no orders; the fixture gives it a price in every zone and an app password. Ahmed Gas has orders. SA1 token.
Steps:
1. PATCH /distributors/{City Gas}/code { code: "CY" }.
2. PATCH /distributors/{DA}/code { code: "AH" }.
3. DELETE /stores/{Ahmed Gas Store}.
4. PATCH /distributors/{City Gas}/store with a pin inside South; then with the Outside point.
5. PATCH /distributors/{City Gas}/approve. Sign in as City Gas and keep the token.
6. PATCH /distributors/{City Gas}/suspend with no reason; then { reason: "Test suspend" }. After 60 seconds, call GET /distributors/me with City Gas's token. Then try to sign in as City Gas again.
7. PATCH /distributors/{City Gas}/approve with no body; then with { reason: "Test reactivate" }. Sign in as City Gas.
8. GET /audit-logs?distributorId={City Gas}.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 200 with code "CY"; codeLocked false.
2. Step 2: 409 DISTRIBUTOR_CODE_LOCKED ("The shop code can't change after the first order."). DA keeps AG, and GET /distributors/{DA} shows codeLocked true.
3. Step 3: 409 STORE_IN_USE ("This store belongs to a shop and can't be removed.").
4. Step 4: South gives 200 with store.zone South; the Outside point gives 422 STORE_OUTSIDE_ZONES and the store doesn't move.
5. Step 5: City Gas becomes ACTIVE.
6. Step 6: no reason gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED; with the reason, City Gas is suspended and its old token gets 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED within 60 seconds; signing in again gets 403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE "This account isn't active. Call the office."
7. Step 7: no body gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED naming reason (reactivating needs one); with the reason, 200 and City Gas is ACTIVE, and the sign-in succeeds.
8. Step 8: rows distributor.code_change, distributor.store_update, distributor.suspend (with the reason) and two distributor.activate rows (the second with from SUSPENDED and the reason), all by SA1.
Spec ref: ADR-01, ADR-22; API_CONTRACT §7.3 (PATCH code, store, approve, suspend), §7.2 (DELETE /stores/:id), §3.3 (sessions), Appendix B

Title: The office live map gets a fresh token and reconnects when the /drivers socket refuses it

Title: A refill is one size and 1 to refill.maxCylinders cylinders: 30 by default, 31 refused

2. As SA1, GET /api/v1/zones/city/<Lahore id>.

Expected result:
1. Step 1: exit code 0.
2. Step 2: three active zones with the file's shapes (valid, area above 0).

Title: Shop app sign-in: a plain form with no code option, a tidy phone number and clear refusals
Role: DISTRIBUTOR (Ahmed Gas); a driver login for one step
Preconditions: Shop app on a test phone, signed out. You have Ahmed Gas's mobile number and password, and Kashif's driver login. The office phone (support.phone) is set.
Steps:
1. Open the app. Read the sign-in screen.
2. Type Ahmed Gas's number with a space or a dash in it, then tap the Password field.
3. Type a wrong password and tap "Sign in".
4. Type the right password. Tap "Show", then "Hide".
5. Tap "Forgot password? Call the office". Come back to the app.
6. Clear the fields. Sign in with Kashif's driver number and password.
7. Sign in as Ahmed Gas with the right password.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: the title "Sign in" with "For shops using Smart Fleet"; the fields "Mobile number" (with +92) and "Password"; a "Sign in" button. No language buttons, no code or OTP option, and no raw words such as "signIn".
2. Step 2: the number now reads like "0300 1234567".
3. Step 3: the button shows "Signing in…", then "Wrong phone number or password." shows under the form. No pop-up box. The words "OTP" and "one-time code" never appear.
4. Step 4: the password shows and hides.
5. Step 5: the phone's dialler opens with the office number.
6. Step 6: "This account is for the Smart Fleet Driver app." No home screen opens.
7. Step 7: Home opens with "Salam, Ahmed Gas" and the balance.
Spec ref: ADR-03; API_CONTRACT §2.1 (no OTP wording), §2.3 (AUTH_*), §7.1; UX_MOBILE S1, §3.2, §3.6 (WrongApp gate)
Notes: Repeat once on the driver app (subtitle "For Smart Fleet drivers").

Title: The phone's API client turns failures into stable codes and refreshes an expired session once
Preconditions: Unit tests of apps/mobile/src/api/client.ts and errors.ts with a mocked HTTP adapter and the real English resources.
Steps:
1. Make one call time out after 15 seconds; make another fail with no response at all.
2. Return 503 { code: "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE" }; then 500 with no body; then 409 with no code.
3. Fire three calls at once that all get 401, with POST /auth/refresh succeeding once.
4. Repeat step 3 with the refresh failing.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: ApiError codes NETWORK_TIMEOUT ("This is taking too long. Check your signal and try again.") and NETWORK_OFFLINE ("No internet connection. Check your signal and try again."), both retryable.
2. Step 2: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE "The service is busy. Please try again in a minute." (retryable); INTERNAL_ERROR (retryable); UNKNOWN "Something went wrong. Please try again." No raw server text or HTTP number is ever the message.
3. Step 3: exactly one POST /auth/refresh call. The new refresh token is stored, and each of the three calls is retried once and succeeds.
4. Step 4: the session is cleared and the Toast "Please sign in again" shows once.
Spec ref: API_CONTRACT §2.3 (General, Client-only), §7.1 (refresh with reuse detection); UX_MOBILE §3.1 (API client v2: timeouts, error normalisation, single-flight 401 refresh), §3.2
Notes: The website client (UX_ADMIN §1.7) needs the same single-flight test in apps/admin-web/src/api/__tests__/client.spec.ts.

Title: A fresh database migrates from empty to the current schema with no drift
Preconditions: An empty PostGIS 16 database (postgis/postgis:16-3.4) and an empty shadow database, with a role allowed to CREATE EXTENSION.
Steps:
1. In apps/api, run npx prisma migrate deploy.
2. Run npx prisma migrate status.
3. Run npx prisma migrate diff --from-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --to-migrations prisma/migrations --shadow-database-url <shadow> --exit-code (the schema is the FROM side, as in CI: DATA_MODEL §2.5).
4. Query pg_extension, the table list, expense_types and _prisma_migrations.
5. Start the API on this database and GET /api/v1/health.
Expected result:
1. Step 1: 0_baseline and then inc1a_foundations apply without error.
2. Step 2: "Database schema is up to date".
3. Step 3: exit code 0 (no difference).
4. Step 4: postgis, uuid-ossp and pgcrypto exist. The inc1a tables exist (distributor_zone_prices, distributor_zone_price_sizes, app_settings, stored_files, expense_types). The six expense types are there. _prisma_migrations has both rows, with finished_at set.
5. Step 5: 200 with status ok.
Spec ref: ADR-19; DATA_MODEL §0, §2.2, §2.3, §2.4 (backfills safe on an empty database), §2.5 (ci.yml), §3.3, §3.4, §3.8 (invariants 12 and 14, on an empty database)
Notes: A database-level test in the e2e suite (real database, no HTTP apart from the health check). With only 0_baseline applied, DATA_MODEL §2.3 expects 38 tables.

Title: Migrating a copy of the old database gives every distributor a code and correct counters
Preconditions: A database built from the af889bf schema with prisma db push, loaded with a legacy fixture: three distributors without codes, created on 1, 2 and 3 Oct 2026. The first has 12 orders and 4 BANK_MANUAL top-ups, the second has none, the third has 1 order.
Steps:
1. Run prisma/scripts/migrate.sh with the repo at the baseline release, then again at the inc1a release.
2. Query distributors (code, next_order_no, next_topup_no, next_refill_no, next_cylinder_no), orders.order_no and payments.request_no.
Expected result:
1. Codes are D01, D02 and D03 in created_at order, and each matches ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,5}$.
2. next_order_no is 13 for D01, 1 for D02 and 2 for D03. next_topup_no is 5 for D01 and 1 for the others. next_refill_no and next_cylinder_no are 1.
3. order_no runs 1 to 12 for D01 in (created_at, id) order, with no gaps or repeats; request_no runs 1 to 4.
4. The CHECK constraints distributors_code_chk and distributors_counters_chk exist and hold.
Spec ref: ADR-19; ADR-22; DATA_MODEL §2.3, §3.2 (Distributor), §3.4 (backfills 1, 2 and 5, CHECK constraints), §3.8 (invariants 1–3 and 14)

Title: After migration every distributor's ledger adds up to its cached balance
Preconditions: Legacy fixture: D01 has a cached balance of Rs 5,000 and ledger rows summing to Rs 4,500 (a CREDIT_TOPUP of Rs 6,000 and a keyless DEBIT_ORDER of Rs 1,500). D02 has Rs 0 and no rows. D03 has Rs 2,000 and no rows. D04 has Rs 100 with rows summing to Rs 300.
Steps:
1. Run migrate.sh up to inc1a.
2. Query ledger_entries and the ledger sum per distributor, and audit_logs for wallet.opening_entry.
3. Run the nightly check query from DATA_MODEL §3.6 (or WalletService.verify).
4. Start the API and, as D01's user, GET /api/v1/wallet/statement.
Expected result:
1. D01 gets one ADJUSTMENT of +Rs 500 (+50000) with reason_code OPENING_BALANCE and key opening:<D01 id>. D03 gets +Rs 2,000. D04 gets −Rs 200. D02 gets none.
2. Every ledger row has an idempotency_key; old rows use legacy:<id>.
3. For every distributor the ledger sum equals advance_balance_paisa. The nightly check returns no rows and raises no WALLET_CHECK_MISMATCH alert.
4. One wallet.opening_entry audit row per opening entry, with actor_kind SYSTEM and actor_label migration:inc1a.
5. D01's statement shows an "Opening balance" item.
Spec ref: ADR-06; ADR-11; API_CONTRACT §1.4 (StatementKind OPENING_BALANCE), §5.4 (invariant), §8.5 (wallet-nightly-check, checklist step 6); DATA_MODEL §1 (rule 2), §3.4 (backfills 6 and 7), §3.6 (Nightly wallet check), §3.8 (invariants 4–5); Appendix B (wallet.opening_entry)
Notes: Ops checks each opening entry against the bank before the pilot (SET-002).

Title: Every expense gets a type, and the six standard types exist
Preconditions: Legacy fixture with expenses in categories FUEL (3 rows), MAINTENANCE (2), OTHER (1), FOOD (1) and RENT (1). No TRAVEL expenses.

Expected result:

2. Archived types LEGACY_FOOD "Food" and LEGACY_RENT "Rent". No LEGACY_TRAVEL, because no expense uses it.
3. No expense has a NULL type_id: FUEL → Petrol, MAINTENANCE → Maintenance, OTHER → Other, FOOD → Food (archived), RENT → Rent (archived).
4. distributors and ledger_entries are unchanged by this step.
5. The API lists the six active types and the archived ones marked archived.
Notes: The legacy categories at af889bf are FOOD, UTILITIES, LABOUR, FUEL, MAINTENANCE, RENT, OFFICE, TRAVEL, EQUIPMENT and OTHER.

Title: Customer phones become +923XXXXXXXXX, or stay as typed and are flagged for fixing

Spec ref: API_CONTRACT §7.4 (rule 1); DATA_MODEL §3.4 (backfill 10), §3.5 (duplicate phones pre-check), §3.8 (invariant 11); Appendix B (client.phone_needs_fix)
